title: Fresh Paste Friday
genre: UK freakbeat (1966-67 mod and psychedelic beat)
subject: A bill-poster pastes gig posters onto the same hoarding by the bus station every Friday morning and finds each one peeled off by Monday, so he starts printing an extra copy for the girl who clearly wants it on her bedroom wall.
caption: UK freakbeat, 1966-67 mod beat drive, driving 4/4 with tambourine on the off-beats. Jangling Rickenbacker twelve-string guitar, a snarling fuzz-toned lead guitar in short riffs, a Farfisa organ playing pumping chords, a punchy melodic bass, and a fast snare-heavy drum kit with crash accents. 1967 London studio texture, compressed and punchy, spring reverb, slightly raw and fast. Male lead, bright nasal tenor, mid-high register, cheeky and punchy, with group shouted backing on the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 138 BPM, A major. Jaunty, cheeky, a little love-struck. No drum machine, no synth pads, no autotune, no modern pop gloss, no slow ballad sections.
lyrics:
[Intro - fuzz guitar riff and Farfisa, drums crash in]

[Verse 1]
Friday morning, bucket and brush
Wet paste dripping, in a rush
Stick the band to the hoarding wall
Bus station, wall to wall

[Chorus]
Fresh paste Friday, hey hey hey
Somebody takes my poster away
Fresh paste Friday, one for the wall
One for the girl I haven't met at all

[Verse 2]
I printed an extra, tucked in my coat
Rolled it up with a rubber band and a note
"Hope it's not creased, hope it's not torn
See you Friday at the bus-stop door"

[Chorus]
Fresh paste Friday, hey hey hey
Monday morning, the hoarding's grey
But there's a cup of tea on the kerb for me
And a note that says "Same time next week"

[Bridge - organ and fuzz riff]
Stick it on, hold it down
Best poster in the town

[Chorus]
Fresh paste Friday, hey hey hey
She turned up with a mug and a tray
Fresh paste Friday, one for the wall
One for the girl who came to stay

[Outro - fuzz guitar and Farfisa, crash ending]
Fresh paste Friday, hey hey hey
Fresh paste Friday, hey
